standard.title: Specification for Copper Rods and Bars for General Engineering Purposes
standard.sector: Metallurgical Engineering / Copper and Copper Alloys

sectional_committee.name: Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, tolerances, chemical composition, mechanical properties, workmanship, finish, sampling, and testing of copper rods and bars intended for general and industrial engineering applications. It covers rods and bars in round, square, rectangular, and hexagonal shapes manufactured through extrusion, drawing, cold or hot rolling, forging, casting, or a combination of these.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, tolerances, chemical composition, mechanical properties, workmanship, finish, sampling, and testing of copper rods and bars intended for general and industrial engineering applications. amendments.summary: Incorporates reference updates: substitutes IS 1387:1993 for the legacy general metallurgical supply standard; substitutes IS 3288 (Part 3):1986 for legacy wrought terminology; substitutes IS 1608:1995 for metallic tensile testing; and substitutes IS 2826:1986 for dimensional tolerances on copper alloys rods and bars.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Copper Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all copper rods and bars supplied for general engineering purposes must conform to IS 4171:1983 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Medium and large-scale enterprises had to comply by October 19, 2024, small enterprises by January 19, 2025, and micro enterprises by April 19, 2025. Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified engineering copper rods in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial copper bars.
requirements: Every commercial tag or label attached to bundles/coils of copper rods and bars, along with the accompanying test certificate, must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The standard covers rods and bars across four geometries: a) Round Bars/Rods; b) Square Rods/Bars; c) Rectangular Rods/Bars; d) Hexagonal Rods/Bars. Sizing bounds are as declared by the manufacturer for the scope of the licence.

The surface of the rods and bars must be clean, smooth, bright, and completely free from harmful defects such as severe scratches, cracks, inclusions, pitting, or oxidation scale. Non-coiled rods must be reasonably straight and free from twists.
To ensure dimensional accuracy for machining and assembly fits, the diameters or widths across flats must stay strictly within the tolerances defined in IS 2826.

When required by the purchaser to verify suitability for welding, brazing, or high-temperature processing under reducing atmospheres, specimens must undergo the Hydrogen Embrittlement test. Samples heated in a hydrogen atmosphere at 900°C must show zero microscopic or macroscopic surface cracking or blistering.
For factory audits, a sample size of 5 pieces of 5 cm length is required for chemical testing, and a 1-meter length of bar/rod is required for physical/mechanical tests.

The control unit (lot) comprises all copper bars/rods of the same size, shape, condition, and manufactured through the same manufacturing process from the same cast of raw material in a day. One random sample is tested from each heat/cast for chemical composition, and one sample per control unit for tensile properties.
